summary: Discovery call: Halo Robotics is evaluating migration from OpenAI-hosted endpoints and in-house vLLM/TGI experiments to Redwood Dedicated or Private. Primary drivers are cost predictability, lower tail latency, and data residency/compliance. Discussed compatibility concerns (prompt/eval parity), kernel/quantization differences, routing/fallback, and security (KMS, SOC2, SSO). Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, security docs, schedule pilot.
topics: vLLM/TGI eval parity and inference differences
security and private deployment (KMS, SSO, audit logs)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 37 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Rina Gupta (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Halo CTO), Lena Ortiz (Halo ML Eng), Maya Flores (Halo Security Lead)

[00:00] Alex Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, happy we could get the Halo team together. quick intros?
[00:08] Samir Patel: yeah hi i'm samir, cto at halo, we run the inference stack and i'm driving the evals for migration.
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: lena, ml eng, i've been working on fine tuning and also testing vLLM in our infra.
[00:20] Maya Flores: maya, security lead, i'll be focused on data residency and KMS questions.
[00:26] Alex Park: great. rina is our se, she'll run through performance stuff. rina?
[00:31] Rina Gupta: hey all, yeah i'll cover latency, throughput, batching, and some compatibility notes. quick high-level — you mentioned you're currently on openai for prod and tinkering with vLLM/tgi in-house?
[00:44] Samir Patel: correct. openai for most customer-facing flows, but costs spiked and tail latency is a problem for some workflows. we've spun up vLLM and TGI experiments to reduce cost and control latency, but parity isn't there yet.
[01:00] Alex Park: totally reasonable pattern. curious on scale — what are you seeing in tps and seq lengths?
[01:06] Samir Patel: baseline is about 20 rps for chat features, peak bursts to ~200 rps during certain workflows. avg seq is 120 tokens, but the retrieval path sometimes pushes 700 token histories.
[01:19] Lena Ortiz: and we do a lot of function-calling style prompts plus structured JSON outputs, so any differences in tokenizer or function-calling behavior break our downstream parsers. we've already seen subtle differences between openai and anthro-type models.
[01:35] Rina Gupta: okay that's helpful. on the dedicated side we typically recommend reserved GPU pools sized for your 200 rps peaks with autoscaling for bursts. latency SLOs we aim for are p95 under 150ms for 120-token requests on optimized models — depends on quantization and batching.
[01:53] Samir Patel: interesting — what about eval parity? we don't want regression on prompt quality when moving from openai to redwood-hosted models or to self-hosted variants.
[02:03] Alex Park: good question. two parts: model family and prompt engineering. we provide a model catalog and can run side-by-side benchmarks — exact parity is hard if you're using proprietary gpt-s style models, but for open models we try to pick variants with matched temperature/llm configuration. we also recommend running your eval suite on our infra to compare logits/outputs.
[02:22] Lena Ortiz: when you say "our infra" — do you mean hosted or dedicated? will the same model and weights run identically on dedicated vs hosted vs private?
[02:30] Rina Gupta: the runtime is the same core, but there are small differences due to kernel selection and quantization. seq length and kv-cache handling is consistent; however, bit-exact parity isn't guaranteed across quantized kernels (int8/int4) and different runtimes like vLLM can produce different tokenization edge cases. we surface value choices and recommend the evaluation plan.
[02:53] Maya Flores: security question — can dedicated be deployed in our VPC? and we need KMS/HSM integration for keys and audit logs for models.
[03:03] Alex Park: yes Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. for Private deployments we offer customer-managed control plane and on-prem options. KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, HSM via partners) are supported; we also provide audit logging and RBAC. we'll share the security pack.
[03:20] Samir Patel: good. one concern — network egress and residency. some of our clients require EU-only. can we pin regions?
[03:27] Rina Gupta: yes, you can pin deployments to regions and we support data residency controls in Private. Dedicated can be provisioned in target regions too.
[03:34] Lena Ortiz: on the vLLM/TGI side, our ops folks are seeing memory fragmentation and unstable kv-cache under long context loads. do you have recommendations?
[03:44] Rina Gupta: memory fragmentation on vLLM is a common pain; our runtime optimizes KV cache pooling and has continuous batching to reduce memory pressure. we also have recommendations for sequence bucketing and prompt truncation. for very long contexts we support offloading strategies and chunked KV fetch.
[04:03] Samir Patel: sounds promising. another question — how much work to switch API surface? we use OpenAI-compatible calls heavily.
[04:11] Alex Park: we provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for easier migrations but also a richer Redwood API. compatibility layer covers common endpoints, function-calling, and streaming, but there are edge cases — we'll help map your integration and highlight any changes.
[04:28] Lena Ortiz: function-calling nuance is real — we've had differences in argument coercion between providers, which caused mismatch in downstream parsers. can you run our sample prompts through your compatibility shim?
[04:39] Rina Gupta: absolutely, that's part of the pilot. we'll run your sample prompts and the eval set. we'll collect diffs and a pass/fail matrix.
[04:47] Maya Flores: on compliance: SOC 2, ISO? do you have certifications for Dedicated/Private?
[04:53] Alex Park: Redwood as a company has SOC 2 Type II. Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to meet customer compliance needs; for Private you can do on-prem to satisfy stricter audits. we'll share our compliance pack and references.
[05:07] Samir Patel: what's the pilot timeline look like? we'd like to see a small pilot in 1–2 weeks if possible.
[05:12] Rina Gupta: we can start with a 1-week benchmark: day 0 onboarding and infra touchpoints, day 1–3 baseline runs (openai vs dedicated), day 4–6 load tests and long-context tests, day 7 results + tuning.
[05:25] Samir Patel: good. what about cost model for Dedicated? we need predictable unit economics to compare to openai's per-token.
[05:33] Alex Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity, monthly commit with clear throughput targets. unit cost typically drops with higher commits and quantization. we'll provide example TCO models based on your traffic profile.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: and for eval parity do you support running our automated eval suites (BLEU/ROUGE/F1 or custom metrics)?
[05:52] Rina Gupta: yes we can run custom evals; we can also instrument token-level logs and differences, and attach regression alerts to prompt sets.
[06:02] Samir Patel: any gotchas with tokenization? we saw a case where a contract id split tokens differently and broke matching logic.
[06:09] Rina Gupta: tokenization differences can happen across model families; we recommend canonicalizing identifiers (escape sequences) or running a pre-tokenization check. we'll include tokenizer mapping notes in the evaluation.
[06:21] Alex Park: quick pivot — are you considering Anthropic? you mentioned earlier.
[06:25] Samir Patel: we have a trial on anthro for safety properties, but cost again is higher and we worry about lock-in.
[06:33] Rina Gupta: same compatibility story applies; we can emulate many open model behaviors but proprietary models have different priors.
[06:39] Maya Flores: encryption in transit and at rest — can we bring our keys?
[06:44] Alex Park: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) supported for Private and Dedicated integrations with cloud KMS; HSM path for Private as needed.
[06:53] Samir Patel: great. a concrete question: will your dedicated/runtime run our existing TGI model weights as-is? we tested TGI locally.
[07:03] Rina Gupta: we onboard TGI and vLLM-style models frequently. supported model formats include standard LLM weights. there can be conversion steps for certain weight formats and quantization; we'll handle that in onboarding.
[07:17] Lena Ortiz: and what about latency tail under bursts? our issue is p99 spikes during concurrent KV cache warming.
[07:25] Rina Gupta: we address warmup with pre-warming and elastic burst pools; plus prefix caching to reduce recomputation. p99 targets depend on model size and quantization but we can tune batching policies.
[07:37] Samir Patel: ok. ops question: what's the rollout path? we want a canary then gradual traffic shift.
[07:44] Alex Park: we support canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback policies. console gives per-route dashboards and per-token cost insights.
[07:55] Maya Flores: who owns the SLA? if we sign a dedicated contract, what's uptime and support?
[08:00] Alex Park: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and a support tier for faster incident response; specific numbers and SLOs in the contract. we'll include SLA terms.
[08:09] Samir Patel: let's talk bench specifics — we'll provide 5 representative prompt sets including long context retrieval, structured output, and instruction-following. can you run them with openai baseline and dedicated with quantization and also on our vLLM setup?
[08:24] Rina Gupta: yes that's the plan. we'll run openai baseline (your account) and our dedicated variants, and we can also help run against your vLLM/TGI infra if you provide access or share logs.
[08:36] Lena Ortiz: timeline? we want results before next sprint planning in two weeks.
[08:42] Rina Gupta: we can aim for a 1-week benchmark window starting next week, then 3 days to analyze results.
[08:50] Alex Park: ok i'm going to recap and call out deliverables.
[08:54] Alex Park: Alex -> send Dedicated pricing/examples; Rina -> benchmark plan + sample prompts; Maya -> security questionnaire + KMS reqs; Samir -> traffic profile and prompt sets. any other asks?
[09:08] Samir Patel: that's it. also can you include a note on model quantization tradeoffs and which models you recommend for our use case?
[09:16] Rina Gupta: yes i'll include model recommendations and expected perf/cost for int8 vs int4.
[09:22] Maya Flores: and please include SOC2 evidence and audit points for Dedicated.
[09:26] Alex Park: yep. we'll send the security pack and a short onboarding checklist.
[09:31] Samir Patel: sounds good. thanks.
[09:33] Alex Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with next steps and calendar for pilot kickoff.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional overlap and short pauses; some product names transcribed as v l l m or t g i. We will attach benchmark plan and security pack as links in follow up email.
